sources.entry: claude-intercom by MuhammadTalhaMT - Relays messages between two Claude Code sessions on separate machines using the Channels API, with delivery tracking and per-message reply budget. Pairs sessions belonging to different accounts, which native cross-session messaging does not. Although this sort of functionality is now a platform feature, it's always cool to see people who have built their own so

summary.one_liner: A two-way bridge that relays messages between Claude Code sessions on different machines (possibly different people's accounts) over HTTP, delivering them as channel notifications.
summary.what_it_does: Runs as an MCP server (intercom.ts, via npx or Bun) that declares the Claude Code channel capability and starts an HTTP listener. A send_message tool POSTs a message to the other machine's intercom, authenticated with a shared secret in an X-Intercom-Secret header. The receiving session gets the message as a channel notification tagged with its id and can reply with replyTo set. A check_message tool reports whether each outbound message is sent, delivered-to-process, or answered, with per-message expectReplyWithin deadlines. The README says the body is schema-validated (size and character limits) and that a GET /health endpoint is unauthenticated. Messages are not persisted.
use_cases: Let a backend and frontend developer's Claude sessions ask each other questions across machines
Relay code review findings from one Claude session to another developer's session
Coordinate Claude sessions working on different packages in a monorepo
Push CI/CD build results into a running Claude Code session via webhook
Connect Claude sessions across a Tailscale network, ngrok tunnel, or VPN
how_to_run: npx -y claude-intercom (configured as an MCP server in .mcp.json with MY_ROLE, REMOTE_HOST, INTERCOM_SECRET, INTERCOM_PORT)
openssl rand -base64 32 (generate a shared secret; use the same value on both machines)
export INTERCOM_SECRET='...' in the shell that launches Claude Code
Alternative from source: git clone, cd claude-intercom, bun install, then use command bun with args pointing to intercom.ts
notable: Pairs sessions belonging to different people or accounts, which the README says native cross-session messaging cannot do
Three-state delivery tracking (sent, delivered-to-process, answered) via send_message and check_message
Per-message reply deadlines via expectReplyWithin rather than one global timeout
Works across OSes and cloud providers (Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry) per the README, with direct HTTP instead of Anthropic-relayed messages
Config can reference ${INTERCOM_SECRET} so the secret stays out of the committed .mcp.json
caveats: Shared-secret auth only: secret is sent as plaintext header, so it must run over Tailscale, HTTPS, or another encrypted transport; no replay protection
Inbound messages can inject text into a Claude session; the README says this is not enforced by a real permission boundary, so pair only with trusted peers
Requires the --dangerously-load-development-channels flag and a stdio-attached session; not usable as a remote-hosted MCP server
